title: Property Damage Liability — Henderson Family v. QuickShip Logistics Ltd.
facts: On October 12, 2025, a delivery truck operated by QuickShip Logistics Ltd. lost control on Maple Street and crashed into the front porch and living room wall of the Henderson family residence at 42 Maple Street. The driver, employed by QuickShip for 2 years, was making a routine delivery in clear weather conditions. Police reports indicate the driver was not under the influence but was exceeding the residential speed limit of 25 mph by approximately 15 mph. The Hendersons were not home at the time but their property sustained significant structural damage estimated at $85,000 by an independent assessor. Personal property damage (furniture, electronics, family heirlooms) is estimated at $35,000. The Hendersons also claim $15,000 in temporary housing costs while repairs are made, and $20,000 in emotional distress damages. QuickShip's insurer has offered $60,000 in settlement, which the Hendersons rejected as inadequate. QuickShip argues the damage estimate is inflated and that some claimed items were pre-existing damage.
supporting_materials: Police report from October 12, 2025 documenting the accident and speed violation. Independent structural damage assessment ($85,000). Personal property inventory with photographs and receipts where available. Temporary housing receipts totaling $15,000. QuickShip driver employment records and vehicle maintenance logs. Insurance adjuster's initial assessment ($60,000 offer). Neighbor testimony regarding property condition before the accident.
